transcript.text: It sounds like your washing machine may be struggling with an unbalanced or unevenly distributed load. Try redistributing the laundry inside the drum to ensure it is spread out evenly before starting the spin cycle again. From what you have described, the most likely cause is unbalanced / uneven load. Does it keep turning slowly backwards and forwards as if trying to balance the load, and does it spin fine with a different, evenly-spread load?
yeah it sloshes back n forth, tries to speed up then slows down a few times then gives up. it was just one big heavy bath mat on its own tho, full load yesterday spun fine

This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Machines deliberately skip or reduce the spin when a load is unbalanced (one heavy item, a small load, a duvet or a bath mat). Clothes then come out wet. It would be worth a closer look if it never spins even with a normal mixed load, or it hums without draining. Is the drum empty of water when it tries to spin, or is there water still in it?
drum is empty of water, just the wet mat in there. drained fine
Next: Check the machine is level and (if recently moved) that the transit bolts are removed. Let me know what you find.
it doesnt rock, sits steady. not been moved either
From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
